msItem.title: Continuous gloss
msItem.note: A continuous gloss to a copy of the psalms (ff. 5-250v) and canticles (ff. 251-74) of the Roman version. Latin text and OE gloss (Ker, Anglo-Saxon, p. 11).

provenance.orgName: Winchcombe, Gloucestershire, Benedictine abbey of St Kenelm
provenance.p: This attribution was rejected in the second edition of Medieval Libraries of Great Britain (1964), which did not change in the Supplement (1987). No corresponding Medieval Libraries of Great Britain index card was found during data reconciliation work in 2026. Compare Ker, Anglo-Saxon, p. 12: Perhaps from Winchcombe, since in the litany Kenelm's name is in majuscules (like the names Mary, Michael, Peter, and Benedict) and he precedes the other English martyrs, Oswald, Edmund, and Alban.

provenance.orgName: Canterbury, Kent, Benedictine cathedral priory of Holy Trinity or Christ Church
provenance.p: This attribution was rejected in the second edition of Medieval Libraries of Great Britain (1964), which did not change in the Supplement (1987). No corresponding Medieval Libraries of Great Britain index card was found during data reconciliation work in 2026. For comparison, this attribution is not mentioned in the catalogue description in Ker, Anglo-Saxon, p. 11-12.

history.provenance: Given by Archbishop Parker to Sir Nicholas Bacon, the Lord Keeper, and by Bacon to Cambridge in 1574 (f. 1). (Ker, Anglo-Saxon, p. 12).
Old Cambridge marks are D. 3. 4 and 256 (Ker, Anglo-Saxon, p. 12).
